table.name: Friend
table.purpose: Friendship edges between high schoolers: each row states that the student with student_id considers the student with friend_id a friend. Both columns reference Highschooler.ID; the pair (student_id, friend_id) is the natural key. Related table Likes presumably stores crush/like relationships between the same students.

friend_id.name: friend_id
friend_id.description: ID of the high schooler who is the friend in the relationship; references Highschooler.ID. Together with student_id it forms the friendship pair (student_id lists friend_id as a friend).

student_id.name: student_id
student_id.description: ID of the high schooler who has the friend; references Highschooler.ID. Each row means this student lists friend_id among their friends (the relationship is not necessarily symmetric in this table).

table.name: Highschooler
table.purpose: A roster of high school students: one row per student with a unique ID, grade level (9-12), and first name. It is the entity table referenced by the Friend (friendship edges between students) and Likes (which student likes which) tables, forming a small social-network schema.

ID.name: student_id
ID.description: Unique numeric identifier for each high school student; primary key of the table. Referenced by Friend.student_id, Friend.friend_id, and Likes.liked_id in the related tables.

grade.name: grade_level
grade.description: The student's grade level (year) in high school, ranging 9-12 (freshman through senior).

name.name: name
name.description: The student's first name (given name). Not unique — e.g. Gabriel and Jordan each appear twice.

table.name: Likes
table.purpose: Edge table in a high-school social network: each row records that one highschooler (student_id) likes another (liked_id), a directed many-to-many relationship between Highschooler records. Complements the Friend table (presumably mutual relationships) with one-directional 'likes'.

liked_id.name: liked_id
liked_id.description: ID of the highschooler being liked (the target of the affection). References Highschooler.ID.

student_id.name: student_id
student_id.description: ID of the highschooler who expresses the like (the source). References Highschooler.ID, though the profiler did not detect the join. Flagged as primary key by the profiler, but since a student can like multiple people, the true key is likely the pair (student_id, liked_id); treat the PK detection as an artifact of the small sample.
